response:
Diagnosis after five generations: the family is converging and the design axes are now measurable. Conjunctive_CashYield_Runway (FMB 5.84, alpha +6.0% t = 3.76, Sharpe 0.472) beats its additive twin on every metric, so the interaction is genuinely multiplicative — averaging lets extreme cheapness offset insolvency, which is exactly the trap. CashYield_WorstCase_Solvency shows demonstrated-resilience (five-year minimum runway) is at least as good as the current level (FMB 5.92). CashYield_With_Claims_Turnover produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.610) at full coverage but only +2.6% alpha, meaning revenue-productivity-of-claims adds raw spread quality but is partly factor-spanned. Two negative lessons to respect: enriching the distress side additively with re/lt cut the alpha nearly in half, and embedding claims in the price denominator (liquidity-adjusted EV) destroyed the signal. So this generation crosses the multiplicative structure with the best distress variants and tests two new distress channels (accrual concealment, flow coverage of claims) inside that structure.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_WorstRunway
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm is compensated value only if it has never lacked a claim-adjusted liquidity buffer in recent memory, so cheapness should be multiplied by demonstrated worst-case solvency rather than by a possibly window-dressed current snapshot.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This crosses the archive's two strongest ingredients — the multiplicative rank structure that lifted alpha to +6.0% and the five-year minimum runway that gave the strongest FMB slope — so it directly tests whether their contributions are additive in evidence. The worst-case statistic also stabilizes portfolio composition, which should raise Sharpe relative to the current-level conjunctive version.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Triple_Conjunctive_Cheap_Solvent_Productive
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)), RANK(RATIO(revt, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Survival requires both a liquidity stock and an operating flow large relative to claims, so a firm that is cash-cheap, liquid against its liabilities, and generating substantial revenue per unit of liabilities is the cleanest possible healthy-cheap firm, while failure on any one leg marks a trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Claims turnover delivered the archive's highest Sharpe (0.610) at full coverage, and the conjunctive structure delivered the highest alpha, so combining the two as a strict three-way conjunction should preserve alpha while improving spread quality. Unlike the failed additive enrichment with retained earnings, multiplication cannot let a strong leg mask a fatal weakness on another.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: StrictMin_CashYield_Runway
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: The binding constraint on a cheap firm's return is its weakest dimension, so the return-relevant score is the minimum of cheapness and claim-adjusted liquidity rather than their product.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The product and the minimum encode different economics — the product still rewards an extreme on one axis while the minimum is governed purely by the bottleneck — and separating them is the cleanest way to learn what the multiplicative gain in gen 4 actually came from. This is deliberately a single-axis design test against Conjunctive_CashYield_Runway, holding both channels fixed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Conjunctive_SmoothedYield_Runway
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable cash-generating capacity, measured over three years, is the valuation input that should be interacted with solvency, because a one-year cash windfall or shortfall misclassifies precisely the distressed firms whose cash flows are most erratic.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Smoothing improved the FMB slope in the additive family while leaving alpha essentially unchanged, so testing it inside the superior multiplicative structure tells us whether horizon and structure improvements compound. It should also reduce month-to-month rebalancing of the long leg, a Sharpe-relevant diagnostic.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_LowAccrualBuild
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms approaching distress conceal deterioration by building working capital — stuffing receivables and inventory — so a cheap firm whose working capital is expanding relative to its claims is a trap, while a cheap firm shrinking working-capital investment is converting operations into cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This introduces an earnings-quality distress channel that is a flow-of-accruals concept rather than another solvency level, so it is unlikely to be spanned by RMW or CMA and should add alpha where levels were absorbed. Scaling the working-capital change by total liabilities keeps the claim-relative normalization that has been the consistent discriminator in this archive, and using wcap rather than the oancf-minus-earnings accrual definition preserves full coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Conjunctive_CashYield_FlowAndStock_Solvency
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(pi, lt), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Solvency has a flow leg — pretax profit available to service claims — and a stock leg — liquid assets net of current obligations relative to claims — and a cheap firm needs both, since profitable firms can still fail on liquidity and liquid firms can still erode their cushion through losses.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Enriching the distress side additively hurt when the added channel was retained earnings, a slow-moving stock variable largely redundant with book equity, whereas pretax-income coverage of claims is a current flow measure that is economically complementary to the liquidity stock. Placing the enriched solvency score inside the multiplicative structure tests whether the earlier degradation came from the added channel itself or from additive dilution of the interaction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
